title: Cut an exact blackjack payout off a stack of real-size casino chips and set it beside the bet
instruction: The player has blackjack. Pay the bet with chips from your stack, set beside it.
context: The difficulty is physical: cutting an exact count of 3.3 mm chips off a stack. A dealer pays a winning bet by taking chips off the top of the working stack and setting them down as their own stack beside the bet. With true-size chips the pinch must land inside one chip's thickness (a window of about +/-1.6 mm) for exactly six to come away, and the six must be carried and set down without toppling and without touching the bet. The bet is never moved or capped (no chip placed on it), so surveillance can still read the wager: a capped or moved bet, a chip tipped past 30 degrees or a chip off the table is a procedure error, and a chip left loose (anywhere but the payout or the working stack) costs half the credit. The arithmetic is routine and printed on the layout: BLACKJACK PAYS 3 TO 2, paid in the bet's own colour, so the 4-chip bet is paid 6 chips. Done by: gambling dealers (O*NET 39-3011.00; https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/39-3011.00).
setup: Station tabletop z=0.7475 m; x forward (toward the player), y left, metres; arm bases (0,+/-0.305,0.75); all yaw 0. Fixed green wool felt cloth layout, 2 mm thick, 360 x 550 mm, covering x 0.12-0.48, y -0.45 to +0.10 (felt top z=0.7495), friction 0.40 static / 0.35 dynamic. Printed on the felt in white ink (print only, nothing to touch): a 90 mm betting circle with a 3 mm line centred at (0.300,-0.240); a second, empty betting circle at (0.300,-0.090); and BLACKJACK PAYS 3 TO 2 in 12 mm capitals centred at (0.240,-0.165), facing the player. Chips: 24 identical red $5 casino chips, clay composite (compression-moulded clay and resin), discs 39.37 mm (1.55 in) across and 3.302 mm (0.130 in) thick, 10.0 g each, with a white edge stripe; friction 0.40 static / 0.35 dynamic chip on chip and chip on felt; contact offset 0.5 mm, rest offset 0. The player's bet: 4 chips stacked on the felt in the circle, axis (0.300,-0.240). The dealer's working stack: 20 chips stacked on the felt, axis (0.200,-0.380). Every chip is its own dynamic rigid body; chip k (0 = bottom of its stack) starts with its centre at z = 0.7495 + (k+0.5) x 0.003302 m (each level spawned 0.02 mm apart, closed by the 0.5 s settle before the first observation). Chips are never jittered one by one. Nothing else is on the table. Full collider table, print geometry and sources: README.md.
scoring: Scored from chip poses (a top photo, a side photo and a ruler; the trial's video for violations). A chip is flat when its face is within 10 degrees of level; a flat chip is on level k when its centre is within 1.5 mm of 0.7495 + (k+0.5) x 0.003302 m (level 0 rests on the felt). A stack is a flat level-0 bottom chip plus flat chips on levels 1 to K-1, exactly one per level, each with its centre within 19.685 mm (one chip radius) horizontally of the chip below it; a flat chip within 10 mm horizontally of the bottom chip's axis that is not in the stack (off every level, or a second chip on a level) makes the stack malformed. A stack is neat when every chip's centre is within 10 mm horizontally of the bottom chip's axis, untidy otherwise. The bet's axis and top face are measured where the bet stands: its top chip's centre, and that chip's top face (13.208 mm above the felt at the start; the bet stays within 2 mm of its start or the trial scores 0, see bet disturbed). Payout: the stack of non-bet chips whose bottom chip's axis is 39.37-54.37 mm from the bet's axis, i.e. an edge gap of 0 to +15 mm; there must be exactly one such stack and no other non-bet chip within 64.37 mm of the bet's axis. Working stack: every other non-bet chip must be in one neat stack whose axis is within 30 mm of (0.200,-0.380); a chip in neither is loose. Violations are checked at every control step and kept for the rest of the trial (putting things back never clears them): capping, any part of a non-bet chip over the bet's top face and at most 2 mm above it (at most 15.208 mm above the felt for an unmoved bet), whatever the chip's tilt, where over the top face means horizontally less than 19.685 mm from the bet's axis (inside its rim) for a flat chip and less than 20.185 mm (the rim plus 0.5 mm) for a chip tilted more than 10 degrees: a chip resting on the bet, overhanging its top (a payout chip any amount over the bet's rim at the bet's top height), pressed onto it, or leaning on its top or rim from the felt or from another stack, even for one step (a chip carried more than 2 mm above the bet's top is not capping); bet disturbed, any bet chip's centre more than 2 mm from its starting centre, or tilted more than 5 degrees; knocked over, any chip tilted more than 30 degrees; off the table, any chip centre below z=0.7275 m or outside x -0.19 to 0.91, y -0.65 to 0.65. Any violation: 0. Otherwise, from the end state: 1.0 for a neat payout of exactly 6 chips with no loose chip, both grippers released (each gripper's centre point between the pads at least 30 mm from every chip's bounding box) and every chip still (over the last 1 s no chip's centre moved more than 1 mm and no chip's tilt changed more than 1 degree, judged from poses), all held for 1 s; 0.5 for a neat payout of 6 still held, moving, or with a chip left loose; 0.25 for an untidy payout of 6 (a chip more than 10 mm off the bottom chip's axis but still overlapping the chip below) or a payout of 5 or 7, neat or untidy (mispaid by one chip, over or under); 0 for no payout, a payout of 4 or fewer or 8 or more, a malformed payout, two stacks beside the bet, or a stray chip near the bet. No best-score latch; success is 1.0, and the trial ends after 1 more second at 1.0.
reset_notes: Restack the 4-chip bet in its circle and the 20-chip working stack at its spot, neat and flat, before each trial. Nothing is consumed. The chips are never jittered one by one.
fidelity: True-size chips (Nevada Reg. 12.040: 1.55 x 0.130 in), 10 g, as rigid sharp-edged cylinders; real chips have slightly rounded edges and edge inserts, drawn as a visual stripe. Chip and felt friction 0.40/0.35 is an estimate, not a measurement. The felt is a rigid 2 mm sheet and the printing is visual only. Distances are compressed to the arm's reach; one player, no cards or chip tray. The gripper pads keep the simulator's default material.
